node.title: The h_r dictionary, forced common support, and the p*(d) law
node.closure: structural classification of the column-far band (with one POSED law separated out)
node.statement: For a column-far pencil whose two syndromes come from errors on a common support, with e_0 = 1 and e_1 = L there and d = deg L <= rho, h_r = rho + d and dim K_0 = r + 1 - rho - d, independently of the support size (h_r = 2rho when the ratio is not polynomial or has degree d > rho -- the stacked matrix has only 2rho rows, scope-corrected at wiring with saturation exhibits on record). Common support is forced rather than assumed: any column-far pencil with two bad slopes is generated by two errors on S_1 u S_2, reconstructed explicitly as e_0 = (gamma_2 u_1 - gamma_1 u_2)/(gamma_2-gamma_1), e_1 = (u_1-u_2)/(gamma_1-gamma_2). LB1 is the unique h_r = rho+1 structural family and its type-1 count is forced: d = 1 gives |W| = r+1 exactly, an injective ratio, and hence T_1 = r+1 with zero accidentals. Separately POSED (not proved): the extended law p*(d) = max(rho+d, floor((R+1+d)/2)), which holds 205/210 in the source bank with five named failures, all the symmetric-T quadratic at the H2 shape (n=22, k=11, rho=2, r=9), measured 6 against predicted 7 at 5/5 fields; p* is therefore not a function of (R, rho, d) and must not label strata, and its converse is refuted since p* = 6 at both h_r = 3 and h_r = 4.
